label: Figure 1-1
description: Places data science in the context of data-driven decision making and other organizational data processes; the surrounding text defines DDD as basing decisions on data analysis rather than intuition alone.

label: Figure 2-1
description: Two-phase diagram. The upper mining phase transforms historical data with known class labels into a model. The lower use phase applies that model to a new item whose class is unknown and outputs class accepted with probability 0.88.

label: Figure 2-2
description: CRISP-DM process diagram with business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, and deployment arranged as an iterative cycle; the figure emphasizes iteration rather than a one-pass linear process.

label: Figure 3-1
description: Supervised classification terminology: training examples have predictor attributes and a known categorical target; a learned predictive model estimates the unknown target for new examples.

label: Figure 3-2
description: Twelve stylized people for a classification example. Yes/No labels above heads are target values; head shape, body shape, body color and similar visual properties are predictor attributes.

label: Figure 3-3
description: Entropy curve for a binary class as p(+) varies from 0 to 1. Entropy is zero at p(+)=0 and 1, reaches its maximum 1.0 at p(+)=0.5, and is approximately 0.88 for a 70/30 split.

label: Figure 3-6
description: Default entropy chart for the complete Mushroom dataset. The entropy is 0.96, represented by shading 96 percent of the area across the full dataset proportion.

label: Figure 3-7
description: Entropy chart after splitting the Mushroom dataset by GILL-COLOR. Each bar width shows that value's prevalence and its height shows entropy; total shaded area is the weighted entropy and is lower than the unsplit dataset.

label: Figure 3-8
description: Entropy chart for SPORE-PRINT-COLOR. Some values such as chocolate yield zero-entropy bars, but together they cover only about 30 percent of the population.

label: Figure 3-9
description: Entropy chart for ODOR. Many odor values create zero-entropy partitions; only no-odor has substantial entropy. ODOR reduces total entropy to about 0.1, for information gain about 0.86.

label: Figure 3-14
description: Classification tree resulting from the successive body-shape, head-shape and body-color partitions shown in Figures 3-11 through 3-13.

label: Figure 3-15
description: Instance-space view of a classification tree. Black dots are Write-off cases, plus signs are non-Write-off cases, and shaded regions show how tree leaves partition the population.

label: Figure 3-16
description: Laplace smoothing chart. Probability estimates for observed ratios corresponding to 100%, 80%, and 66% approach their raw ratios as the number of instances increases; smoothing has strongest effect at small sample sizes.

label: Figure 3-17
description: Bar chart ranking churn attributes by information gain: HOUSE 0.0461, OVERAGE 0.0436, LONG_CALLS_PER_MONTH 0.0350, LEFTOVER 0.0136, INCOME 0.0101, AVG_CALL_DURATION 0.0089, HANDSET_PRICE 0.0076, SATISFACTION 0.0003, COLLEGE 0.0000, USAGE_LEVEL 0.0000.

label: Figure 3-18
description: Classification tree learned from cellular phone churn data; the surrounding evaluation reports 73 percent accuracy on the same training data and questions whether that number is trustworthy or useful.

label: Figure 4-7
description: Iris Setosa and Iris Versicolor plotted by Sepal width and Petal width with two learned linear boundaries. Logistic regression separates all shown examples; the SVM boundary is between clumps but misclassifies the starred point at (3,1).

label: Figure 4-8
description: Maximal-margin classifier: two parallel dashed lines form the widest separating bar between classes, and the SVM decision boundary is the solid center line.

label: Figure 4-9
description: Comparison of loss functions versus distance from the decision boundary for a negative instance. No loss occurs on the correct negative side; wrong-side points are penalized, with hinge loss increasing with distance.

label: Figure 4-10
description: Sigmoid curve translating linear score f(x), or distance from the boundary, into class probability between zero and one; uncertainty is highest near the boundary.

label: Figure 4-11
description: Sample cell-nuclei image from which the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset was derived, courtesy of Nick Street and Bill Wolberg. Images were labeled benign or malignant by expert diagnosis.

label: Figure 4-12
description: Iris plot with added nonlinear feature Sepal width squared. Logistic regression and SVM receive the extra feature and form curved nonlinear boundaries; a starred Versicolor point appears near Sepal width 4 and Petal width 0.7.

label: Table 3-1
description: Mushroom attributes include VEIL-TYPE: partial, universal; VEIL-COLOR: brown, orange, white, yellow; RING-NUMBER: none, one, two; HABITAT: grasses, leaves, meadows, paths, urban, waste, woods; EDIBLE target: yes or no.

label: Table 3-2
description: Churn variables: COLLEGE asks whether the customer is college educated; INCOME is annual income; OVERAGE is average overcharges per month; LEFTOVER is average leftover minutes per month; HOUSE is estimated dwelling value; HANDSET_PRICE is phone cost; LONG_CALLS_PER_MONTH is average number of calls lasting 15 minutes or more; AVERAGE_CALL_DURATION is average call duration; REPORTED_SATISFACTION is reported satisfaction; REPORTED_USAGE_LEVEL is self-reported usage; LEAVE is the target asking whether the customer stayed or left (churned).

label: Table 4-3
description: Wisconsin Breast Cancer attributes: RADIUS is mean distance from center to perimeter; TEXTURE is standard deviation of grayscale values; PERIMETER and AREA describe the mass; SMOOTHNESS is local variation in radius lengths; COMPACTNESS is perimeter squared divided by area minus 1.0; CONCAVITY is severity of concave contour portions; CONCAVE POINTS is their count; SYMMETRY measures nuclei symmetry; FRACTAL DIMENSION is coastline approximation minus 1.0; DIAGNOSIS is malignant or benign.

label: Table 4-4
description: Logistic-regression weights ordered high to low include SMOOTHNESS_worst 22.3, CONCAVE_mean 19.47, CONCAVE_worst 11.68, SYMMETRY_worst 4.99, CONCAVITY_worst 2.86, CONCAVITY_mean 2.34, RADIUS_worst 0.25, TEXTURE_worst 0.13, AREA_SE 0.06, TEXTURE_mean 0.03, TEXTURE_SE -0.29, COMPACTNESS_mean -7.1, COMPACTNESS_SE -27.87, and intercept -17.7.
